correctness.rationale: The ratio (1-z)/(1+s z), s=theta-1, has derivative -theta/(1+s z)^2, giving T'=alpha theta f with f=(1-z)^(alpha-1)(1+s z)^(-alpha-1). The logarithmic derivative yields (1-z)(1+s z)f'=(A+2s z)f, A=2-(1+alpha)theta. In the extension strip 0<s<1 and A≥0, coefficient matching gives (n+1)a_(n+1)=[A+(1-s)n]a_n+s(n+1)a_(n-1); induction includes A=0. When theta≤1 the two factors are individually nonnegative binomial series for alpha≤1, including alpha=1. In both cases |s|<1, so integration gives w_k=alpha theta a_(k-1)/k inside the unit disc and monotone convergence at z=1 yields sum w_k=1. The resulting positive-integer Laplace mixture gives the canonical all-dimensional copula and the conditional exponential sampler, with uniform margins. For alpha>1 the ratio at t=0 is (t/theta) times an analytic function equal to one at zero, so psi'' is negative to leading order. Otherwise above the theta frontier, e^t psi tends to positive w_1 and would force a positive Laplace measure to avoid [0,1) and have an atom w_1 at 1. The residual measure would be nonnegative, contradicting w_2 e^(-2t)+O(e^(-3t)) with w_2<0. This excludes any mixing measure, not just integer ones. The all-dimensional complete monotonicity criterion has the required strict endpoint and monotonicity hypotheses.
